مُؤْخِرُ العَيْنِ , (T, S, A, Mgh, Msb, K, [in the CK مُؤَخَّرها,]) said by AO, (Msb,) or A 'Obeyd, (TA,) to be better without teshdeed, from which observation it is to be understood that teshdeed in this case is allowable, though rare, but Az disallows it, (Msb, TA,) and مُؤْخِرَتُهَا, and ↓ آخِرَتُهَا , (K,) [The outer angle of the eye;] the part of the eye next the temple; (S, A, Mgh, Msb;) the part next the لَحَاظ: (K:) opposed to its مُقْدِم, which is the extremity thereof next the nose: (S, Mgh, Msb:) pl. مَآخِرُ. (Mgh.) You say, إَلَيَّ بِمُؤْخِرِ [He looked at, or towards, me from (lit. with) the outer angle of his eye]. (S.) ―
-b2- مُؤْخِرُ الرَّحْلِ, and مُؤْخِرَتُهُ: see آخِرٌ.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
